## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs to lower-case its key: as written, a value stored under any mixed-case key can never be read back with `get`.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `Cache.set` method and raises `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, with the comment updated to match. It also adds tests for a set/get round trip, the default TTL value and entry expiry.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` stores the entry under `"Alpha"`, but `get("Alpha")` looks up `"alpha"` and returns `None`. This breaks the rule in `app/cache.py:14-15`: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together." — Any caller that uses a mixed-case key always misses the cache, and stale entries collect in `_store` because `get` never deletes them. — Fix: Use `self._store[key.lower()] = ...`, and add a mixed-case key such as `"Alpha"` to `test_set_then_get_round_trip`, which only stores lower-case `"alpha"` and so cannot catch this defect.
